chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt owed to us, and he sells wine and the pigs, and then pays us back. He said, 'There is no harm with it; there is nothing upon you from that.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm with it
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ: there is nothing upon you from that

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay off a debt with money earned from selling wine or pigs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the validity of debt repayment depends on the creditor's acceptance of the currency, not the purity of its source. It highlights the Shia juristic distinction that while wine and pigs are ritually impure (*najis*), their sale is permissible (*mubah*) for non-Arabs or in specific contexts, meaning the money derived from them is considered clean for settling debts. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in commercial transactions, prioritizing the resolution of obligations over the moral status of the debtor's income source.
